meaning: the middle of the night; around midnight

senses.en: the middle of the night, from about midnight into the small hours
the middle of the night, with a clock time after it: 半夜两点 'two in the middle of the night'

examples.zh: 都半夜了，你怎么还不睡？
examples.en: It's the middle of the night. Why aren't you asleep yet?
examples.analysis: 都…了 'already' stresses how late it is: 都半夜了 'it's already the middle of the night', with 半夜 standing alone as the predicate. 怎么 asks 'how come', with surprise or mild reproach, and 还不睡 means 'still not going to bed'.

examples.zh: 孩子半夜生病了，我一晚上没睡。
examples.en: The kid got sick in the middle of the night, and I didn't sleep all night.
examples.analysis: 半夜 before the verb sets the time: 孩子 + 半夜 + 生病了 'got sick in the night', with 了 marking the change. The second clause, 一晚上没睡 'didn't sleep all night', shows the cost; it is a loose, everyday way to say you got no real sleep that night, even though the trouble only started at 半夜.

examples.zh: 别半夜给我打电话，好吗？
examples.en: Please don't call me in the middle of the night, OK?
examples.analysis: A request with 别 'don't'. The time word 半夜 comes right after 别 and before 给我打电话 'call me', because 'when' goes before the action in Chinese. 好吗 at the end softens the request.

collocations.en: in the dead of night (often a complaint)
until late at night (工作到半夜 'work till midnight')

related.en: at night; during the night (any time after dark)
evening; night, the whole night included (一晚上 'all night')

meaning: (after a number) … and over, or more; (in talk) the above

senses.en: after a number: that amount or more (六十岁以上 'aged 60 and over')
the above; what was just said (以上是… 'that is …', closing a talk)

examples.zh: 六十岁以上的人坐车不要钱。
examples.en: People aged 60 and over ride for free.
examples.analysis: 以上 follows the number it qualifies: 六十岁 + 以上 'sixty and over', and the whole phrase + 的 describes 人. In rules and notices 以上 normally includes the number itself, so someone who is exactly 60 rides free too.

examples.zh: 从这儿到机场要一个小时以上。
examples.en: It takes an hour or more to get from here to the airport.
examples.analysis: 以上 goes after the amount, the reverse of English 'over an hour': 一个小时 + 以上. 从…到… 'from … to …' frames the trip, and 要 + an amount of time means 'it takes'.

examples.zh: 以上是我的想法，大家觉得怎么样？
examples.en: So those are my thoughts. What does everyone think?
examples.analysis: Here 以上 means 'the above': it points back to everything the speaker has just said and is the subject of 是. It sounds a little formal, which suits a meeting; 大家觉得怎么样 then opens the floor.

collocations.en: that was … (closing a talk: 以上就是我要说的 'that's all I have to say')

related.en: after a number, 'a bit over': 二十多个 'twenty-odd'

meaning: entrance; way in

senses.en: entrance; the way in (to a building, station, park, car park)
entry point of a road: 高速入口 'expressway on-ramp'

examples.en: Excuse me, where's the entrance?
examples.analysis: 入口 is the subject, and 在 + 哪儿 asks where it is. 请问 'may I ask' is the polite opener for a question to a stranger: a guard, a member of staff, a passer-by.

examples.en: The subway entrance is just up ahead.
examples.analysis: 地铁 + 入口: one noun describes another directly, with no 的, as in 'subway entrance'. 就 adds 'right, just': 就在前边 'is right ahead', which reassures someone who is looking for it.

examples.en: This is the exit, not the entrance.
examples.analysis: 入口 'way in' pairs with 出口 'way out': 入 means 'enter', 出 'go out', 口 'opening'. The 是…，不是… frame corrects a mistake, handy at stations and malls where the doors are signed.

related.en: doorway; just outside the door or gate

meaning: way of doing something; approach; how a dish is made

senses.en: the way someone does or handles something; an approach
how a dish or thing is made; the method or recipe

examples.en: This dish isn't hard to make.
examples.analysis: 做法 here is 'how it's made': 这个菜 + 的 + 做法 'this dish's method', and that method is the subject of 不难 'not hard'. Chinese says the way of making it isn't hard, where English says the dish isn't hard to make.

examples.zh: 我觉得他的做法不太对。
examples.en: I don't think the way he handled it was quite right.
examples.analysis: 做法 is 'the way he handled it', a judgment on what he did. 他的做法 is the subject of 不太对 'not quite right'. Chinese puts the negative in the judgment after 我觉得, where English prefers 'I don't think'.

examples.zh: 这个菜还有别的做法吗？
examples.en: Is there another way to make this dish?
examples.analysis: 这个菜 sets the topic first. 还有 'is there also' + 别的 'other' + 做法 asks whether the dish can be made a different way, and 吗 makes it a yes/no question. If you mean a way out of a problem, say 还有别的办法吗 instead.

collocations.en: how to cook a dish; the recipe

related.en: a way out; a solution to a problem

meaning: safe and sound; without accident or harm

senses.en: safe and sound; unharmed (of people, a journey)
peaceful and well, as a wish (祝你平安 'wishing you safety and peace')

examples.en: Is everyone in your family safe?
examples.analysis: 平安 is the predicate with no 是: 家人 + 都 + 平安 'the family are all safe', and 吗 makes it a question. People ask this after a storm, an accident or bad news, so 平安 here means 'unharmed', not just 'fine'.

examples.en: We're back safe and sound.
examples.analysis: Before a verb, 平安 says how something happened: 平安 + 回来 'come back safely'. 已经…了 'already' marks it as done. This is the message you send to reassure family after a trip.

examples.en: Being safe is what matters most. Don't drive too fast.
examples.analysis: Here 平安 'being safe' is the subject of 最重要 'is the most important': the adjective works as a topic with no change in form. 别开太快 'don't drive too fast' is the request that follows, said to someone setting off by car.

meaning: wristwatch

senses.en: wristwatch, including a smartwatch

measure.note: 一块手表 (also 只 or 个)

examples.en: My watch is five minutes slow.
examples.analysis: 手表 is the subject, and 慢了五分钟 means 'slow by five minutes', with the amount after the adjective. 了 marks that the watch has drifted from the right time. 快了五分钟 would be 'five minutes fast'.

examples.zh: 你这块手表真好看，在哪儿买的？
examples.en: Your watch is really nice. Where did you get it?
examples.analysis: 块 is the usual measure word for a watch: 这块手表 'this watch', and 你这块 points at the one on their wrist. 在哪儿买的 is the 是…的 pattern with 是 dropped, asking where a past purchase was made.

examples.zh: 我没有手表，看手机就行。
examples.en: I don't have a watch. I just check my phone.
examples.analysis: 没有 + 手表 'don't have a watch' is the negative of 有. 看手机就行 'looking at my phone does the job': 就行 means 'that's enough, that works'. The second clause has no subject because it is still 我.

meaning: husband or wife; spouse (mainland usage, a bit formal)

senses.en: spouse: one's husband or wife (mainland China; fairly formal, heard most from older speakers; in Taiwan it can mean 'lover')

measure.note: rarely counted; usually 我爱人, 他爱人

examples.en: Her husband is a doctor too.
examples.analysis: 她爱人 'her husband': like close family words, 爱人 follows the pronoun with no 的. 爱人 itself covers husband or wife; 她 is what tells you it's her husband here. 也 'too' sits before 是.

examples.en: What does your spouse do?
examples.analysis: 你爱人 'your spouse', again with no 的. 做什么工作 'do what work' is the standard way to ask about someone's job. 爱人 lets you ask without knowing whether there is a husband or a wife.

examples.zh: 他爱人不舒服，今天来不了。
examples.en: His wife isn't feeling well, so she can't come today.
examples.analysis: 他爱人 'his wife' is the subject of both clauses. 不舒服 means 'unwell'. 来不了 'can't come': verb + 不了 (liǎo) says circumstances make it impossible, not that she refuses.

related.en: husband, in 我先生 'my husband'; also 'Mr.'
wife, in 我太太 'my wife'; also 'Mrs.'
husband (casual and very common; 老婆 lǎopo is 'wife')

meaning: altogether; in total

senses.en: in total; altogether (before a verb or a number)

examples.en: How much is that altogether?
examples.analysis: 一共 'in total' asks for the sum of everything you are buying. It sits right before the amount question 多少钱; 一共是多少钱 is the fuller form, but at a checkout the short version is very common.

examples.en: There are five of us in total.
examples.analysis: 一共 + number + measure word: 一共五个人 'five people in all'. In a statement like this the verb can drop out; 我们一共有五个人 is the fuller form. A typical answer when a restaurant asks how many are in your party.

examples.en: How many times have you been to China in total?
examples.analysis: 一共 comes before the verb and asks for a running total. 来过 'have come': 过 marks past experience. The count 几次 'how many times' sits after the verb; with a place name it can also follow the place: 来过中国几次.

related.en: together, doing something with others; in shop talk in some regions, 一起多少钱？ also means 'how much altogether', but 一共多少钱 is the safe form

meaning: full name (surname + given name), mainly on forms

senses.en: full name, surname plus given name (forms, lists, official use)

examples.zh: 请在这儿写上您的姓名。
examples.en: Please write your full name here.
examples.analysis: 姓名 is the form word for 'full name', so this is what a receptionist or a nurse says when handing you a form. 写上 'write onto': 上 after the verb adds the idea of putting it on the paper. 您 is the polite 'you'.

examples.en: Do I have to fill in both my name and my phone number?
examples.analysis: 姓名和电话 'name and phone (number)' comes first as the topic, and 都 'both' then covers the two items. 要写吗 'need to write?' asks what the form requires. On a form, 电话 means the number.

examples.en: The name on the ticket was written wrong.
examples.analysis: 票上的姓名 'the name on the ticket' comes first as the thing affected, and 写错了 'written wrong' follows, with no word for who wrote it; 错 after the verb gives the result. 姓名 fits because it is the name printed on a document; for your name in general, say 我的名字.

related.en: name; the everyday spoken word (你叫什么名字？)

meaning: bottle; jar

senses.en: bottle or jar: the container itself, empty or full

examples.en: What's in this bottle?
examples.analysis: 瓶子 + 里 'in the bottle': Chinese adds a place word after the noun where English puts 'in' before it. That place phrase is the topic, and 是什么 'is what' asks about the contents.

examples.en: There's no water left in the bottle.
examples.analysis: The place phrase 瓶子里 starts the sentence, and 没 + 水 says what isn't there (没 is short for 没有 here). 了 at the end marks a change: there was water, and now there isn't.

examples.zh: 你能帮我打开这个瓶子吗？
examples.en: Could you help me open this bottle?
examples.analysis: 瓶子 is the object of 打开 'open'. 你能帮我 + verb + 吗 is a polite request: 'could you help me …?'. For an amount of a drink, Chinese uses 瓶 as a measure word instead: 一瓶水 'a bottle of water'.

collocations.en: a bottle of water (瓶 as measure word)

related.en: bottle of: 一瓶水, 两瓶酒

meaning: teacher (as an occupation or job title)

senses.en: teacher, as a profession or job title (forms, news, school staff)

measure.note: 一个教师; more formally 一名教师

examples.en: My mom is a secondary-school teacher.
examples.analysis: 教师 names the profession: X + 是 + 中学 + 教师, with no word for 'a'. This is how you state someone's job. To speak to a teacher, though, you call them 老师, not 教师.

examples.zh: 这个学校的教师都很年轻。
examples.en: The teachers at this school are all young.
examples.analysis: 这个学校的教师 'this school's teachers' is the subject, followed by 都 'all' + 很年轻. 教师 suits talk about the staff as a group; 老师 would also work here and sounds more everyday.

examples.en: Do you want to be a teacher?
examples.analysis: 当 + job means 'to work as': 当教师 'be a teacher', with 想 'want to' before it. In conversation 当老师 is more usual; 教师 sounds more like a job title.

related.en: teacher; the word you use to address one

meaning: the sea; the ocean

senses.en: the sea; the ocean, the open sea as a whole

examples.en: I really want to go and see the sea.
examples.analysis: 大海 is the object of 看: 去看大海 'go and see the sea'. 很想 'really want': 很 adds real force here. 大海 is the sea as a wide, open expanse, the thing people go to look at.

examples.en: Have you ever seen the sea?
examples.analysis: 见过 'have seen' uses 过 for experience: has this ever happened to you? 大海 is the object, and 吗 makes it a yes/no question. A natural thing to ask someone who grew up far inland.

examples.en: My place isn't far from the sea.
examples.analysis: 离 'from' measures distance: A + 离 + B + 远 or 近. Here A is 我家 'my home', B is 大海, and 不远 'not far' is the negative.

collocations.en: look at the sea; go and see the sea

related.en: sea (also in names: 上海, 黄海)

meaning: to form; to make up (a group, a whole)

senses.en: to form (a group, a team) by bringing people or parts together
由 A 组成 'to be made up of A'

examples.zh: 我们三个人组成了一个学习小组。
examples.en: The three of us formed a study group.
examples.analysis: 组成 takes the new group as its object: 组成 + 一个学习小组 'form a study group', and the people who form it are the subject. 了 marks the forming as done. 我们三个人 'we three' puts the number after 我们.

examples.zh: 两个字可以组成一个词。
examples.en: Two characters can make up a word.
examples.analysis: Here the parts are the subject: 两个字 + 可以 + 组成 + 一个词 'two characters can form one word'. The parts come first and the whole comes after 组成. A typical line when someone explains how Chinese words work.

examples.zh: 我们几个同事组成了一个篮球队，你也来吧！
examples.en: A few of us at work have formed a basketball team. Come and join us!
examples.analysis: 组成 + 一个篮球队 'formed a basketball team': the new group is the object, and 了 marks it as done. In casual talk people often use the lighter verb 组 instead: 组了个篮球队. 你也来吧 'you come too' turns the news into an invitation.

related.en: group; to put together (组一个队)

meaning: to visit and look around a place; to tour

senses.en: to visit and look around a place (a museum, factory, school, hospital)

examples.zh: 明天我们去参观一家医院。
examples.en: Tomorrow we're visiting a hospital.
examples.analysis: 参观 + place: the object is where you go to look around, here 一家医院 (家 is the measure word for businesses and institutions). It means looking around a place, as on a tour; to visit a person, use 看: 去看朋友.

examples.en: Can we look around here?
examples.analysis: This time 参观 has no object: 这儿 'here' is the topic, and 可以…吗 asks permission. You might ask this at a gate, a lab or a temple hall.

examples.zh: 欢迎大家来我们公司参观！
examples.en: You're all welcome to come and visit our company!
examples.analysis: 欢迎 + people + 来 + place + 参观: 'welcome everyone to come to our company and look around'. The place sits after 来, so 参观 itself needs no object. A standard line from a host.

related.en: to visit a person: 去看朋友

meaning: vehicles as a group; formal word used on signs and in announcements

senses.en: vehicles as a group (a formal word for signs, rules, announcements)

examples.en: Vehicles can't park here.
examples.analysis: 车辆 'vehicles' is the subject; 不能 'can't' + 停在这儿 'park here' (停 covers both 'stop' and 'park'). A guard or a loudspeaker uses 车辆 because it covers every kind of vehicle at once; between friends 车 is the normal word.

examples.zh: 早上学校门口车辆特别多。
examples.en: In the morning the traffic outside the school gate is really heavy.
examples.analysis: 车辆 + 特别多 'especially many': 车辆 is a collective word for vehicles in general, so it usually goes with amount words like 多 rather than with a number. For a specific number, people switch to 车 with its measure word: 三辆车 'three cars'.

examples.en: Vehicles this way, please.
examples.analysis: 车辆 addresses drivers as a group, the way a guard, a sign or a loudspeaker does; between friends you would just say 车. 请 'please' + 从这边 'from this side' + 走 'go': the route comes before the verb, where English puts it after.

collocations.en: vehicles from outside, not registered there (on gate signs)

meaning: to travel for pleasure; to go sightseeing

senses.en: to travel for pleasure; to go on a trip (去 + place + 旅游)

examples.en: We're planning a trip to Beijing.
examples.analysis: The place goes between 去 and 旅游: 去 + 北京 + 旅游 'go to Beijing to travel', with 打算 'plan to' first. 旅游 does not normally take a place right after it, so say 去北京旅游, not 旅游北京.

examples.en: Do you like traveling alone?
examples.analysis: 旅游 is the activity being liked: 喜欢 + 一个人旅游. 一个人 'one person', placed before a verb, means 'alone, on your own'. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

examples.zh: 今年太忙了，没时间去旅游。
examples.en: This year's been too busy. I haven't had time to travel.
examples.analysis: 没时间 + 去旅游 'no time to go traveling': the verb phrase after 时间 says what the time would be for. 太忙了 'too busy' gives the reason first, and the subject 'I' is dropped because it is obvious.

related.en: to travel; a journey (not only for pleasure)
to visit and look around a place

meaning: anniversary: number + 周年 counts full years since an event

senses.en: anniversary; a full year since an event (十周年 'tenth anniversary')

examples.zh: 今天是我们认识十周年。
examples.en: Today marks ten years since we met.
examples.analysis: Number + 周年 counts full years: 十周年 'the tenth anniversary'. What it is the anniversary of comes before it: 我们认识 'we met, got to know each other'. 是 links 今天 to that date.

examples.zh: 公司五周年，大家一起吃个饭吧。
examples.en: It's the company's fifth anniversary. Let's all have a meal together.
examples.analysis: 公司 + 五周年 'the company's fifth anniversary', with no 的. 周年 is for institutions, couples and events; a person's age uses 岁. 吃个饭 with 个 makes the meal sound casual, and 吧 makes it a suggestion.

examples.zh: 下个月我们来中国就一周年了。
examples.en: Next month it'll be a year since we came to China.
examples.analysis: 一周年 'one full year' marks time since an event: 我们来中国 'we came to China'. 就…了 says a point is about to be reached: 'it will then be a year'. 下个月 sets the time first.

related.en: birthday (for a person's own date, not 周年)

meaning: workplace, employer (mainland usage); unit of measurement

senses.en: workplace; the organization you work for (mainland China)
unit of measurement (米 'meter' is a unit of length)

examples.en: Is your workplace far from here?
examples.analysis: 单位 is the mainland word for the organization you work for: a hospital, a school, a company or a government office. People say 我们单位 / 你们单位 'our / your place', since a workplace belongs to a group. 离这儿远吗 asks about distance.

examples.zh: 明天单位要开会，我去不了。
examples.en: There's a meeting at work tomorrow, so I can't go.
examples.analysis: 单位 here works like 'at work': it is the topic, with no 在, and 要开会 'is having a meeting' follows. 去不了 'can't go' says something else is stopping you.

examples.en: I changed employers last year.
examples.analysis: 换 + 单位 'change workplace', that is, move to a new employer. 了 after 换 marks the change as done, and 去年 'last year' sets the time before the verb. 换工作 'change jobs' is close, but 换单位 stresses the employer.

meaning: picture; image (photo, drawing or graphic)

senses.en: picture or image: a photo, drawing or graphic, often on a screen or page

examples.en: Send me the picture.
examples.analysis: 图片 is put first as the topic, then 发给我 'send to me'. Putting the object first is normal in speech when both sides know which picture is meant. 吧 makes it a friendly request.

examples.zh: 这些图片是你自己做的吗？
examples.en: Did you make these images yourself?
examples.analysis: 这些 'these' + 图片 needs no measure word. 是…的 asks how or by whom something was done: 是你自己做的 'made by you yourself'. 图片 covers drawings and graphics, not only photos.

examples.en: The picture's too small. I can't see it clearly.
examples.analysis: 图片 is the subject of 太小了 'too small'. 看不清楚 'can't see clearly': verb + 不 + result says the result can't be reached. The second clause drops both 'I' and 'it'.

meaning: film; movie (more formal than 电影)

senses.en: film; motion picture (listings, reviews, announcements); in Taiwan also the everyday word for a video clip

examples.en: What film are they showing tonight?
examples.analysis: 放 'to show, screen' + 影片: whoever runs the cinema or the event is the unstated subject. 影片 sounds a bit formal, as in listings; with friends 电影 is the everyday word.

examples.en: Is the film in Chinese?
examples.analysis: 影片 + 里 'in the film', with the place word after the noun. 说的 'what is spoken' + 是中文吗 'is it Chinese?': 的 turns the verb into 'the thing said'. Worth asking before you buy a ticket.

examples.zh: 这个影片讲的是一个医生的故事。
examples.en: This film tells the story of a doctor.
examples.analysis: 讲的是 'what it tells is': 讲 'tell' + 的 makes 'the thing told', and 是 introduces it. 部 is the standard measure word for a film: 这部影片; in casual speech 这个影片 is also heard.
